open.description: Secret ownership does not propagate through the arithmetic itself; the P-256 engine's transfer window into and out of fixed-width storage remains open.
The constant-time inversion's scratch storage and the operands' normalised limb-count metadata remain the recorded residual.
The ECDSA per-signature allocation count is 254.2 against 29 for the authority; improved from 273.4, not discharged.

The DSO bytes are not committed. Two independent clean rebuilds from the committed c1d25e10d reproduce the digest, so the bytes are bound to the declared source and inputs, but a digest match is not a source-to-binary refinement claim.

The write-back store_coordinate -> limbs::normalise secret-dependent timing branch was removed at source in PFP-20 (store_coordinate now trims with limbs::normalise_branchless) and the four engine-on-path contexts fall to 0 at 553e1b8c. The trim still encodes a length derived from a still-secret coordinate before ladder_post, and downstream BN_num_bits/limbs_from_slice/ladder_post length consumers remain; the relocation after declassification is open (PFP-20-NORMALISE.md).

P256Scalar::admit_be_bytes uses `if ct_ge(...) != 0 { return None }`, a branch on a scalar range check. It is not on the ladder path (tests only today) and the accept/reject outcome is a required public admission decision; removing it would be a correctness bug. Reported, not fixed.

The DSO-bound differential exercises the internal field operations only through EC_POINT_mul and ECDSA, because p256::mont_reduce_into, p256::wide_mul_x86 and limbs::normalise_branchless have no exported entry point. No source-level test is substituted while calling the court DSO-bound.

The passing branch audit resolves mod_exp_core_consttime_from_parts to its _prepared carrier through a verified inline mapping; it cannot distinguish inlining from a source edit producing the same instruction stream, and it maps secret-dependence as a reviewer aid rather than establishing it. The audit is not a constant-time proof.
The venue exposes no PMU and has no frequency, turbo, SMT or isolation control; every timing row is SCOPED_OBSERVATION.

Supersedes PFP2-CTGRIND-TEST-BINARY at 553e1b8c: the DSO-level ctgrind now runs against the candidate artefact. What remains is the instrument limit: memcheck reports conditional jumps/moves on undefined data and cannot distinguish a constant-time cmov from a branch, and the nonce generated inside ECDSA_do_sign has no exported entry point and cannot be tainted. The historical debug-binary reading 3,023/123 stays visible in RESULTS-83f67826.md and is not comparable to the DSO populations.

Supersedes PFP2-MUTATION-CONTROL-NOT-AT-DIGEST at 553e1b8c: the mutation control is measured in the artefact (A 553e1b8c vs B 86bc63a6). B is necessarily a different binary, so the control is anchored at the candidate digest but cannot itself be at it; B's semantic equivalence to the authority is 512 points at one seed, not the whole kernel domain.

limits: This record binds the PFP-2 classification and its declared identity; it executes nothing.
It does not establish that the cited campaign occurred as described; the campaign raw output is the record of that.
The candidate DSO bytes are not in the repository; two independent clean rebuilds from the committed source reproduce the digest, but a digest match is not a source-to-binary refinement claim.
The binary branch audit is a review aid: it lists compiler-emitted conditional jumps and their targets; a reviewer maps them to the source's secret classification. It is not a constant-time proof.
The DSO-level ctgrind is a taint run: memcheck cannot distinguish a cmov from a branch, and the library RNG nonce cannot be tainted.
The DSO-bound differential cannot call the internal field kernels directly; it exercises them only through the exported EC and ECDSA surface.
The 19.2234x and 19.3228x readings are the same instrument at two different digests; the change is not a trend and the venue drifted by a comparable amount.
A green validation is a statement about claim form, not about the truth of the measurement.

scope.security_profile: candidate distribution-shaped libcrypto.so.3 at digest 553e1b8c against the recorded OpenSSL 3.6.4 authority; the P-256 engine and the branchless write-back trim change only the P-256 scalar path, so only ecdsa256 is expected to move

threat_model.observation_model: wall-clock latency on a virtualised host; no PMU, no cache or branch counters, no frequency, turbo or SMT control
threat_model.statement: P-256 private scalars and ECDSA nonces are SECRET_DATA; the field prime, the group order and the base point are public. The P-256 field engine uses masked add, subtract, select, cswap and conditional subtraction with fixed loop counts, and store_coordinate now trims with a branchless normalise; the DSO-level taint run reports 0 engine origin contexts at 553e1b8c. The write-back still encodes a length derived from a secret coordinate, which is a named residual. Neither the taint run nor the branch audit is a constant-time proof.
